cells.tense: The work of steadying someone else's momentum is running clean and easy right now.
cells.ask: Before the week ends, take one thing you're already keeping going and give it one more room or one more person. Nothing new to start.
cells.core:
You're the one keeping something moving when letting it drop would be easier. That isn't force. You pace it, you handle it, you don't burn yourself out — and because you stay in it, other people can stay in it too. On a good day it looks like a long table: someone brings a worry, you take it in without making a thing of it, and by the end the worry has somewhere to go.

One thing to watch. What people notice is that you keep going; what it costs you is quieter — when you carry a direction for someone, your own needs slide down the list. So take one thing you're already keeping going and widen it this week, one more room or one more person, and notice what gets set down while you do.

cells.tense: You are already managing how a conversation that has not happened yet is going to go.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're pushing and leave it alone for two days. If it comes back on its own, good. If it doesn't, that's what you needed to know.
cells.core:
You're holding a direction for someone and pushing harder than the situation asked for. Ahead of you there's a version where it finally lands, where the effort was worth it, and you've been living in that version — so every exchange becomes a chance to move them a step along. The pushing ends up crowding out the closeness it was for; people start managing you back instead of talking to you.

Try this. Pick one thing you're pushing and leave it alone for two days. If it comes back to you on its own, that tells you something. If it doesn't, that tells you more. Letting a thing stand without you goes further than force when you're trying to stay close.

cells.tense: You know how to hold a direction with someone, and lately you are not doing it.
cells.ask: Take one thing that has finished — a plan, a habit, a way you used to show up — and mark it done out loud to one person. Then keep one small promise to yourself the next day.
cells.core:
You know how to hold a direction for someone, and lately you don't. The ability is there; the offering isn't. You wait to be asked now, or you stay a step outside the room where the caring actually happens. Nothing ends on purpose, so the energy that would go into connection has nowhere to land — and the longer it pools, the harder it is to arrive in an ordinary conversation.

Take one finished thing and let it be finished, said out loud to one person. Then keep one small promise to yourself the next day. Small and yours, not theirs — so you can feel the release instead of performing it for anyone.

cells.tense: You are the one steadying people and keeping a direction alive, and you describe it as just what the moment required.
cells.ask: Pick one act you've been filing under 'what needed doing' and say 'this is mine' about it once, out loud to one person, then leave it there.
cells.core:
You keep people steady. You keep a direction alive when quitting would be reasonable. It's in how you show up, what you hang onto for someone, what you refuse to let drop. Yet it gets described as if the situation ran itself, or the group's momentum carried it, or anyone would have done the same.

Here's the piece to claim back. Pick one act you've been filing under 'what needed doing' and say 'this is mine' about it once, out loud, to one person. Not as credit. Just as true. What you carry deserves to be said in your own voice instead of left running in the background.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding it steady, and you haven't said it's yours.

attempts.check: The record supports a person who keeps others' momentum alive through hard stretches and whose warmth of connection is presently doing that work well; it does not support claims about who they care for, what they have sacrificed, or what happened earlier. A reader could reasonably say they are simply reliable and warm in ordinary ways, so no cell should name the particular people, costs or history behind the steadiness. The asks (widen one ongoing thing, wait after saying a hard thing once, let one ending land and keep the small promise, say this is mine about one thing) all survive a wrong read because each teaches something on its own. The sentence that serves the writer is any line implying the person already led or already lost something; it is cut.
